description: Around 1595, two lovers from Verona died in less than five days. Shakespeare condenses a romance into a social tragedy: clan hatred destroys youth.

hero.hook: Five days between love at first sight and death: the most famous love tragedy in the world.

blocks.text: To **1595**, **William Shakespeare** writes . It is known as the greatest love story in theater. In reality, it is also a violent criticism of the hatred inherited between rival families. The two lovers do not die only through bad luck: they pay for the failure of a city incapable of protecting its youth against clan violence. **[[Romeo and Juliet]]**

blocks.caption: The balcony scene: absolute love facing the clans of Verona.

blocks.text: Shakespeare does not invent history. He is mainly inspired by **Matteo Bandello**, an Italian storyteller from the 16th century, himself heir to older stories. Its genius lies in the **condensation**: where the sources spread the action over months, Shakespeare narrows it down to **five days** only. Every minute counts, the catastrophe becomes inevitable.
At Bandello's, Juliet wakes up before Romeo dies. Shakespeare deletes this farewell to make the ending more cruel.

The play begins almost as a comedy, with puns and lively street scenes. Then **Mercutio**, brilliant mind and bearer of , dies in the middle of the story. With it disappears the carelessness: the tone shifts definitively into tragedy. Romeo first played the , in love with Rosalind before discovering a much deeper and more dangerous love. **[[Cynicism]]** **[[Medieval courtly love]]**

sections.title: Shakespearean alchemy: from short story to drama

blocks.text: **Romeo Montague** and **Juliet Capulet** fall in love at a masked ball, at first ignoring each other's names. The balcony scene celebrates love, but also the refusal of the family name: “Renounce your father and abdicate your name. » The secret marriage of **Brother Laurent** was to appease the  between the two clans. **[[Vendetta]]**

blocks.caption: Romeo and Juliet: adolescent passion caught in clan violence.

blocks.text: Within hours, **Tybalt** kills Mercutio, Romeo kills Tybalt in retaliation and is banished from Verona. An epidemic of **plague** delays the messenger responsible for warning Romeo that Juliet is not dead, but only put to sleep by a drink. This is not divine destiny alone: ​​these are trivial coincidences added to an already toxic society. Final suicides affirm absolute freedom where the world no longer leaves room for them.

sections.title: A tragic mechanism: between chance and necessity

blocks.text: The play analyzes vendetta as an engine of destruction. Montague and Capulet hate each other without even remembering why. The prologue speaks of an “old hatred” which produces “new blood”. Juliette, barely **13 years old**, must marry Count **Pâris**; Romeo wanders in a melancholy that his friends misunderstand.

The **Prince of Verona** represents a law powerless against the private militias of the two families. At the end, in front of the bodies of the young people, he accuses the parents: “All are punished. » The lovers are the victims of a system where the honor of the clan prevails over individual happiness. Dante already mentioned the **Montecchi** and **Cappelletti** in the 14th century, two centuries before Shakespeare.

sections.title: Social responsibility and the sacrifice of youth

blocks.text: The influence of the play is immense. Shakespeare mixes religious devotion and physical passion, inventing a new romantic vocabulary for English theater. The Shakespearean  remains a dramaturgical model studied in conservatories around the world. **[[Peripateticism]]**

In the 20th century,  transposes the conflict to New York: the **Sharks** and the **Jets** replace the clans of Verona. The pattern still holds: the love of others clashes with the hatred of the group. Religious, racial or social conflicts constantly take up the Shakespearean matrix. **[[West Side Story]]**

**Romeo and Juliet** condenses into five days an adolescent idyll and a denunciation of inherited violence. Shakespeare shows that absolute love does not survive where society prefers resentment to life.
